Updated BuffBench evaluation scripts (`main.ts`, `main-single-eval.ts`) to run these new Opus agents against benchmark tasks. This change enables testing and deployment of Opus-based agent configurations within the Freebuff agent framework.

eli5.text: The testing system that checks how well the coding assistant works has added a new, more powerful model option to run against. If you looked at the evaluation setup, you would see it now runs three configurations instead of two: the existing strong mode plus the new model variant that reads files more calmly. The change is live for internal testing and benchmark runs, not something end users toggle directly.

ai.title: use-send-message suppresses errors on user-initiated abort
ai.summary: Added `wasAbortedByUserRef` to `cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts` to track user-initiated cancellations. The `abortController.signal` listener now sets this ref to true. In the error handling block, if this flag is true, the function logs the cancellation and returns early, preventing the display of error messages for intentional aborts. This ensures that user-initiated stops do not trigger misleading error UIs.

eli5.text: When you press the stop button while the assistant is answering, the program previously showed a confusing error message. Now it recognizes that you stopped it on purpose and quietly ends the response without showing an error screen. If you use the stop button, you'll no longer see a scary error; the assistant just says it was interrupted.

ai.summary: Version 1.0.532 ships as a release-bump commit on `cli/release/package.json`, advancing the CLI package version from 1.0.531 to 1.0.532 with no code changes in this hunk. This release aggregates same-day work across the CLI surface: Base2 agents gained new `base2-opus` and `base2-opus-chill-on-reading-files` definitions routed through an `opus` mode in `createBase2`, BuffBench evals (`main.ts`, `main-single-eval.ts`) added runs for those Opus agents, the CLI input placeholder in `cli/src/utils/input-modes.ts` now reads 'enter a coding task or / for commands', a new `useUsageMonitor` hook in the Chat component auto-triggers the `usage` input mode when credit thresholds are crossed, and `cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts` gained `wasAbortedByUserRef` tracking so user-initiated aborts log and return early instead of surfacing misleading error UIs. Notable model retuning shipped here includes the max-mode thinker best-of-n workflow switching to `anthropic/claude-opus-4.5` via new `thinker-best-of-n-opus` and `thinker-selector-opus` agents, plus BuffBench judges consolidating to a two-agent `openai/gpt-5.1` and `google/gemini-3-pro-preview` pool. The version bump itself is a
ai.evidence: The commit modifies only `cli/release/package.json` in a one-line hunk, changing the `version` field from 1.0.531 to 1.0.532 with no other code or behavioral changes. Analysis notes confirm this is a pure version bump release-commit with all user-visible work described in the bundled release updates list.

eli5.text: This release upgrades your CLI experience by adding support for new, more capable AI models and making the tool more helpful and polished to use. You now get access to Claude Opus 4.5 in the highest-complexity problem-solving mode, which replaces the previous GPT-5 setup and should deliver stronger reasoning for the toughest coding tasks. The app will now automatically show you a usage warning when your credits get low, so you are less likely to run out unexpectedly mid-sessions. Improvements to slash-command auto-complete and the chat input placeholder make it easier to discover and use built-in commands. When you deliberately stop a running task, you will no longer see confusing error messages pop up. Finally, a new structured way of talking to the web API makes login, publishing, and referral features more reliable and better at explaining actual problems. Upgrading gives you a smoother, more informative, and more powerful coding assistant that just got noticeably smarter at solving harder problems.

Backend `genUsageResponse` and `usage-service.ts` expose `autoTopupEnabled` from `user.auto_topup_enabled` column. `triggerMonthlyResetAndGrant` returns `MonthlyResetResult` instead of `Date`, avoiding redundant queries. eli5.text: If you have auto top-up turned on, you will no longer see the pop-up warning telling you that your account balance is getting low, as long as you still have some credit left. The app now checks whether your card will automatically add more money when you run low, and if so, it stays quiet unless your balance drops all the way to zero. That means the warning banner only comes back when you're truly out of credits, not just when you cross the usual 'getting low' thresholds.

ai.title: CLI 1.0.533 ships key handling, input, and credit warning updates
ai.summary: CLI 1.0.533 ships the same-day consolidations from the Freebuff monorepo CLI surface. The release bundles the new useChatKeyboard hook that centralizes key dispatch through resolveChatKeyboardAction, the ask-user Other field refactored to use the shared MultilineInput component, and the auto top-up-aware low credit warnings exposed via genUsageResponse and usage-service.ts. The version bump itself is a one-line change in cli/release/package.json, with no behavioral changes introduced by this commit alone.
ai.evidence: Version field in cli/release/package.json was incremented from 1.0.532 to 1.0.533. This is a release bump commit that ships the user-visible changes from the same-day preceding commits.

eli5.text: This release smooths out how you type and navigate while working in the command-line assistant, and it tidies up the prompts you see when your account balance runs low. Typing in the chat now handles keyboard shortcuts more reliably, so arrow keys, slash commands, and mention completions behave consistently whether you are moving the cursor, accepting a suggestion, or switching between history, instead of occasionally misfiring or ignoring input. The built-in forms used when the assistant asks you a clarifying question now use the same shared text-entry field everywhere, fixing glitches where multi-line answers, spaces, and backspacing did not work as expected. If you have auto-replenishment turned on, the annoying low-balance banner stops interrupting you while your balance is still positive, because the app now knows your payment method will top up automatically. Together, these changes mean fewer stuck keystrokes, cleaner form responses, and a quieter workspace when your credits renew on their own, so you can keep working without popups or input lag getting in the way.

ai.title: Prevent auto-topup disable on transient errors
ai.summary: Auto-topup no longer disables on transient Stripe or network failures in packages/billing/src/auto-topup.ts. validateAutoTopupStatus and checkAndTriggerAutoTopup now only call disableAutoTopup for AutoTopupValidationError and AutoTopupPaymentError. Other errors return a blocked status or throw without changing the user's setting, allowing retry on next trigger.

eli5.text: When your automatic credit top-up runs into a temporary hiccup like a network timeout or a brief Stripe service issue, it will no longer turn off your auto-top-up setting as a result. Instead, it now only stops the setting when there is a permanent problem like a missing or declined payment method. You would notice this if you tried to check out and saw a message saying your payment method couldn't be verified right now rather than finding your auto-top-up permanently disabled. The change is live today for anyone using the auto-top-up feature.

Previously, only the status text was available, obscuring upstream error details. This change improves debugging visibility for failed API calls within the web client.

eli5.text: When the assistant fails to talk to its AI provider, you now see the exact error message that came back, not just a vague 'something went wrong' note. Previously, internal logs only captured a one-line status like 'Bad Request' without any details about why the request failed. This update makes those logs include the full error text returned by the provider, so debugging problems becomes faster and clearer. It affects anyone investigating why a chat request didn't complete.

ai.summary: Deleted base2-opus and base2-opus-chill-on-reading-files agent definitions; createBase2 mode union narrowed to fast|default|max, model hardcoded to anthropic/claude-opus-4.5, chillOnReadingFiles option removed, and subagent spawn lists simplified. MAX_MODEL_PATTERN in editor-best-of-n.ts swapped two editor-implementor-opus slots for editor-implementor-gemini; best-of-n-selector.ts adds reasoningOptions.max_tokens 4000 when isOpus. Scope: .agents/base2/base2.ts, .agents/editor/best-of-n/best-of-n-selector.ts, .agents/editor/best-of-n/editor-best-of-n.ts, evals/buffbench/main.ts. eli5.text: If you run the automated coding evaluation called BuffBench today, it will test only two assistant configurations instead of four. The two removed variants were extra flavors of the main assistant that used a different model and a setting that made it relax while reading files; the remaining two cover the standard tier and the top tier. The model used to pick between competing code drafts now spends more thinking steps on the top tier, and the top-tier draft-picking sequence now uses a different mix of draft-writing models. Nothing changes for the main coding assistant used in day-to-day work; only the internal evaluation harness is affected.

eli5.text: The specialized helper tools the editor uses to generate and select code suggestions are now always available, instead of only appearing under certain paid-tier conditions. Three specific helper variants that were previously restricted to higher-tier users are now registered permanently in the selection pool. If you use the editor, you may now be offered these previously gated helper variants as part of the suggestion options without changing your account tier.

ai.title: Standardize message content to part arrays in types
ai.summary: Message types in util-types.ts now require content as part arrays instead of strings. AuxiliaryData renamed to AuxiliaryMessageData and exported. Deprecates timeToLive, keepDuringTruncation, keepLastTags in favor of tags. Updates context-pruner.ts and task-researcher.ts to handle array content.

eli5.text: The agent framework now requires every message to carry its text content as a structured list of parts rather than a plain string, so both the system and the tools that prune old messages or search conversation history work consistently. This is a behind-the-scenes standardization: if you write custom agents or message-handling code that still passes text directly as a string, that code must be updated to send it inside a part array, and the old fields for time-to-live, truncation flags, and last-message tags are being replaced by a single 'tags' list. Nothing a typical end user would notice changed in the apps themselves; the update is in place for any developer building agents on this SDK to adopt.

ai.title: SDK run integration test use APIKEYENVVAR
ai.summary: SDK run integration test replace hardcoded '12345' API key with process.env[API_KEY_ENV_VAR]. Fixes test failure when API key missing. Scope: sdk/src/__tests__/run.integration.test.ts. Imports API_KEY_ENV_VAR from @codebuff/common/old-constants.

eli5.text: When the team runs their automated tests to make sure the assistant software still works, those tests no longer rely on a fake, made-up code to log in. Instead, they pull the real login credential from a secure spot that only trusted testers can access. If you happen to watch a test run, you'll see it quietly reads that credential from your computer's protected settings rather than typing in a bogus placeholder. The result is that tests fail less often when the real credential is already set up on the machine running them.
